acceptance_criteria.criterion: PUT /api/config/credentials with { "host": "github.com", "token": "ghp_full" } persists the entry to config.json and updates in-memory config.
DELETE /api/config/credentials/github.com removes the entry from both disk and memory.
Changes take effect immediately for subsequent clone operations (no server restart).
A token shorter than 4 characters is fully masked (e.g., "****").
Request validation rejects missing host or token fields with 400.
Unit tests cover all three endpoints including edge cases and validation.

summary: Created `src/server/routes/config.ts` with `registerConfigRoutes(router, appConfig, configPath?)` implementing GET, PUT, and DELETE for `/api/config/credentials`.
Token masking: last 4 chars with `****` prefix; tokens < 4 chars return `****`.
PUT validates host (non-empty, no path separators/whitespace) and token (non-empty); returns 400 on failure.
DELETE returns 404 if host not found; removes the field from config if map becomes empty.
All mutations update in-memory `appConfig` and persist via `saveConfigField()`.

comments.note: The `host` field validation in PUT rejects path separators and whitespace (security guard against URL injection). This matches the plan's constraint but is not covered by a test for backslash separators — only forward-slash is tested. QA may want to add a backslash test.

`registerConfigRoutes` accepts an optional `configPath` for testability. The `startServer()` function in `server/index.ts` calls it without `configPath` (uses the default `getConfigPath()` from `saveConfigField`). If integration tests ever spin up a full server and want to use a custom config path, they would need to thread `configPath` through `ServerConfig` — this is deferred per the WP scope.

summary: Reviewed 3 files: src/server/routes/config.ts, src/server/index.ts, src/server/__tests__/routes/config.test.ts. 0 Critical, 0 High. Token masking is correct (last 4 chars, full mask for short tokens). Host validation rejects path separators and whitespace. Full token never returned in any API response. All 17 tests pass. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: INFO — A03/A04 (Insecure Design): The host field validation regex /[\s/\\]/ rejects path separators and whitespace but does not block reserved JavaScript property names (__proto__, constructor, prototype). In Node.js >= 18 (project requirement), bracket-notation assignment obj['__proto__'] = value on a plain object does NOT modify Object.prototype — this is V8-safe. However, defence-in-depth would suggest adding /^(__proto__|constructor|prototype)$/ to the rejection check to make the intent explicit and protect against any future JSON.parse round-trip edge cases. Low priority only.

INFO — A09: GET /api/config/credentials exposes last 4 characters of each token plus all configured hostnames. For a local-only tool this is an acceptable trade-off (direct config.json read gives full tokens). No High finding; the exposure is bounded and intentional for usability. Token masking is correctly implemented: tokens shorter than 4 chars return '****', longer return '****' + last 4 chars. Full token not present in any API response (verified by test 'full token value is never present in the response').

No other OWASP A01–A10 issues found. PUT host validation rejects path separators and whitespace; token stored directly without transformation; in-memory mutation is immediate; persistence via saveConfigField() is correct; DELETE uses object key lookup (no filesystem exposure); all three endpoints return only masked credential data in success responses.

[documentation-forward] rest-api.md must be updated with the 3 new endpoints: GET /api/config/credentials, PUT /api/config/credentials, DELETE /api/config/credentials/:host. The DELETE handler reads `host` directly from URL params without trimming or separator validation (unlike the PUT handler which applies host.trim() and the injection-guard regex). In practice URL path params won't carry whitespace, but noting the asymmetry for consistency: if a stricter design is ever wanted, DELETE should apply the same /[\s/\\]/ guard. Not blocking — current behaviour is safe.
